  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwindale Senior Citizen Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are committed
to the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter and spirit
of Local, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private life. We
will be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest. We
will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of morality
and integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We shall refrain
from abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We will inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and equitable
in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions in which
we have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest, or create
a perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
available to the public in general. We shall refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest
in thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to any
other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or censure
of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established.

  Senior Center.

  program, such as allowing activities from home and including staff from the
  Police Department, Library, and Recreation Departments.

To:  Honorable Chair and Commission Members
 From:  Elizabeth Rodriguez, Public Services Director
 Issue:  Update on the Irwindale Community Foundation Request for Donations

Recommendation:

That the Senior Citizen Commission receive an update on a request for donations from
the Irwindale Community Foundation.

Administrative Action:

Submitted by:

 Eloise Beltran, Senior Center Manager
 (626) 430-2286

 Reviewed I Approved by:

 Elizabeth Rodriguez, Public Services Director

Background and Analysis:

At the September 27, 2021 Senior Citizen Commission meeting, Staff presented a report
on a request for donations the Senior Center is requesting from the Irwindale Community
Foundation (ICF) in the amount of $1 ,600 to purchase promotional items for the newly
launched Healthy Irwindale Campaign .

Since that meeting , the Senior Center also added a $5,000 request for donations from
the ICF to help fund new furniture for the back lounge room . Staff is requesting th is
donation to purchase a sofa with a love seat, round tables, padded chairs and some
artwork for the walls.

This room will be used for Adults 50+ to read the newspaper or a book, work on a puzzle
and where the book club will be holding their meetings.

  Page 1
 The following outlines the cost of the items the Senior Center is requesting to purchase
with the ICF Donation:

 Item  Description  Quantity Cost
 Sofa & Love seat  ReadinQ/lounQinQ/puzzle area  1 set  $2,500 .00
 42" Round Table  ReadinQ/puzzle area  1  $1 ,100.00
 4 Padded Chairs  ReadinQ/puzzle area  4  $1 ,100.00
 Art work  Pictures for walls  Various $ 300.00
  Grand Total: $5,000.00

The ICF met on Tuesday, October 19th to review its Fiscal Year 2021/2022 budget and
requests for donations. The ICF approved the Senior Center's request for $5,000 to
purchase furniture for its back lounge room and $1 ,600 to purchase the promotional items
for the Heathy Irwindale Campaign. The City Council is scheduled to accept the donations
from the ICF at its Wednesday, October 27th meeting.
